experiments.reasoning: The passage describes a deliberate procedure involving systematic observation of a phenomenon (the luminous appearance in a pullet) under controlled conditions (darkened chamber) to investigate its cause and compare it to another observed phenomenon (the luminousness of veal). The author explicitly mentions sending meat into the larder and observing its behavior over time, which aligns with the definition of an experiment.
experiments.description: The experiment involved observing a pullet (young hen) that exhibited a light source in its rump region. The author took the pullet from the larder, brought it into a darkened chamber, and noted the luminous spots near or on the rump. The goal was to compare this phenomenon to the earlier observation of luminous veal and to determine whether the light was related to the freshness or other properties of the meat.
experiments.quote: having several nights sent purpoely into the Larder, to observe, whether any Veal, since brought thither, or any other meat, did afford any light, a negative answer was alwaies brought me back; save at one time, which happened to be within less than 48 hours of that, at which the Luminousness of the Veal had been first taken notice of; for at this time there was in the same Larder a conspicuous light seen in a Pullet, that hung up there, which having caus’d to be brought up into a darkned place in my chamber in the night time, I perceived four or five luminous places, which were not indeed near so large as those of the Veal, but were little less vivid than they. All of these I took notice to be either upon or near the Rump, and that, which appear’d most like a Spark of Fire, shone at the very tip of that part.
experiments.outcome: The luminous spots in the pullet were observed, though not as vivid as those in the veal. The pullet was fresh and not foul or ill-sent, indicating that the light was not due to decay or spoilage.
experiments.location: Larder (mentioned in the text) and a darkened chamber in the author's chamber.
